entries.name: CI red on the current head
entries.condition: The CI result for the run's current head commit is anything other than success.
evidence: the CI result and the head SHA it belongs to
entries.next_action: Fix and push a new head; the stop lifts when CI is green on that head.
entries.rationale: Never pass a defect on. Runs stacked on a red head would build on a defect, so they halt with it. Unrelated runs continue.

entries.name: Only stale CI exists
entries.condition: The newest CI result belongs to an obsolete head because a newer head arrived. A result for an older head never counts.
entries.next_action: Wait for CI on the current head; obsolete CI runs are cancelled.
entries.rationale: Stale evidence is not an acceptable buffer. Nothing is wrong with the work, so only this run waits.

entries.name: Sandbox breach
entries.condition: A containment signal fired: a canary path or socket was touched, a forbidden syscall or escape pattern was seen, or the sandbox was found outside its cgroup or network.
entries.next_action: Inspect the snapshot; clear only after the host is judged clean.
entries.rationale: Containment is the assumption every other run relies on. When it fails, siblings on the same host cannot be trusted either, so the fault domain stops.

entries.name: Policy breach
entries.condition: The run did something outside its grant that a denial does not fully absorb: tried to approve its own request, tried to widen its own scope, or acted on an operation after a refusal by another route.
entries.next_action: Review the evidence; decide whether the profile, the policy or the brief was at fault.
entries.rationale: Output of a run that broke its boundary is tainted, so it and everything built on it is frozen.

entries.name: Run token misuse
entries.condition: A run token was presented after revocation or expiry, with a bad signature, from an address other than its run's sandbox, or twice at once from different sources.
entries.next_action: Treat the token as leaked: revoke it, then review how it left the sandbox.
entries.rationale: A token outside its sandbox means a credential-handling failure. Outputs made under it are suspect.

entries.name: Thrash (repeated denials)
entries.condition: The same refused action, or many different refused actions, repeated beyond the profile's threshold within its window.
entries.next_action: Read the denials; adjust the brief, or grant the missing access through an approval.
entries.rationale: A run that keeps hitting a wall is stuck, not progressing. Stopping it saves cost; the work it produced so far is not tainted.

entries.name: Approval flood
entries.condition: A run (or the orchestrator) created more approval requests than its allowance within the window.
entries.next_action: Decide whether the run needs fewer, better-scoped requests.
entries.rationale: Respect for humanity: the approver's interrupt load is measured and capped, and approvals are never batched across different actions.

entries.name: Budget exceeded
entries.condition: Tokens or cost consumed reached the run's budget (task_scope budget in the run token).
entries.next_action: Approve a larger budget for a continuation run, or accept the partial result.
entries.rationale: Plan against actual: the budget is a standard, and exceeding it is an abnormality to look at, not to ignore.

entries.name: Time exceeded
entries.condition: Run wall time reached the budget's minutes, or the run token expired.
entries.next_action: Approve more time for a continuation run, or accept the partial result.
entries.rationale: Same reasoning as BUDGET_EXCEEDED. The token's expiry makes this stop self-enforcing.

entries.name: Resource quota hit
entries.condition: The sandbox reached a hard CPU, memory, disk or process quota, or the host-side cgroup killed a process for it.
entries.next_action: Check whether the profile limits fit the work; rerun with a heavier profile if so.
entries.rationale: A runaway process must become 'that run hit its quota', never a host-wide failure.

entries.name: Host unhealthy
entries.condition: The sandbox host reports low disk or memory, a failed health probe, or a failed dependency such as the proxy or a mirror.
entries.next_action: Fix the host condition; runs resume when the probe is healthy.
entries.rationale: Do not keep working on a broken stack. Pausing, not killing, keeps the work resumable.

entries.name: Ledger integrity failure
entries.condition: A hash-chain verification failed: a gap in seq, a prev_hash mismatch, a bad hash, or an anchor that no longer matches.
entries.next_action: Investigate tampering or a writer fault before any run continues.
entries.rationale: No run proceeds without a tamper-evident record. This is the observability invariant made into a stop.

entries.name: Operator stop (one run)
entries.condition: A human issued the stop command for one run.
entries.next_action: None required; start a new run if the work should continue.
entries.rationale: The kill switch for one run, snapshot kept as evidence.

entries.name: Operator stop (everything)
entries.condition: A human issued the stop-all command.
entries.next_action: Start runs again explicitly once the reason is dealt with.
entries.rationale: The always-visible Stop all. Nothing restarts by itself.
